<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **6** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/data-modeling/fields.mdx`  _(via quote_date (literal, a string literal in replacement))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/relationships.mdx`  _(via quote_date (literal, a string literal in replacement))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **177** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 581ae76a23c6b3ba8e2b69e7d8a920838bc51194` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `fa5ee72f2390efe2d2410ce6e4d73c2e0ffc4277` — the merge of head `9a9f0e6421d9675916ebe74684004b1d3d8f6a00` into base `581ae76a23c6b3ba8e2b69e7d8a920838bc51194`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin fa5ee72f2390efe2d2410ce6e4d73c2e0ffc4277 && git checkout fa5ee72f2390efe2d2410ce6e4d73c2e0ffc4277
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 581ae76a23c6b3ba8e2b69e7d8a920838bc51194 9a9f0e6421d9675916ebe74684004b1d3d8f6a00 && git checkout -B drift-repro 581ae76a23c6b3ba8e2b69e7d8a920838bc51194 && git merge --no-ff 9a9f0e6421d9675916ebe74684004b1d3d8f6a00

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 581ae76a23c6b3ba8e2b69e7d8a920838bc51194
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 581ae76a23c6b3ba8e2b69e7d8a920838bc51194` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c0deeb35cc1bf12b674a57d5490dfe1f4a2ee4bc`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/lint/src/validate-object-field-refs.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.lookup-filter-record-path-structured-refused.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-object-field-refs.test.ts + read, not reviewed: packages/spec/src/data/field-value.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/filter-cross-field-comparison-class.ts, packages/spec/src/data/filter-comparand-type.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.lookup-filter-record-path-multi-valued-refused.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/README.md, packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts.template, packages/spec/src/migrations/chain.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/protocol-version.ts, packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts

Inputs: card #34562 (body and all 7 comments), PR #38096 (body, 5 files, net diff against `main`, merge base f72f3353), the check-runs on the head.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept set, `object-field-ref-unknown` at `lookupFilters[N].value.$record`: a path that resolves and whose head (plain path) or leaf (behind one single-valued hop) is declared with a type in `STRUCTURED_JSON_TYPES` moves from clean to an error. Right. The predicate is the spec's own set, imported and not re-listed, and it is reached only on a path the family's resolution did not already refuse (`!hit`), so no path gains a second finding.
- All seven members, each read in `fieldValueSchema` (`field-value.zod.ts`): `location` and `address` are closed objects; `composite` and `record` are `z.record(string, unknown)`; `repeater` is an array of records; `vector` is an array of numbers; `json` is `z.unknown()`. Six of the seven can never hold one scalar. `json` is the open one: a json column may hold a bare string or number, and for that one stored shape the old accept set could have produced a working comparison. The refusal is still right by declared type: the spec already classes the whole set as `list-or-object`, "not one comparable value" (`filter-cross-field-comparison-class.ts`, the `$field` side of the same comparison), and the server's accepted comparand set is string, number, bigint, boolean, null or Date (`filter-comparand-type.ts`), so an object or a list sent under one of the six scalar operators has no declared reading. Keeping `composite` and `record`, which the card's five did not name, is right.
- Multi-valued verdicts: unchanged. `nonScalar` tests `isMultiValueField` first, and the message interpolates the noun where the literal stood; the pre-existing multi-valued tests are untouched in the diff and green on the head.
- Hop through a structured head (`s_address.city`): still the family's "not a relationship" miss, once. The new `goes through` arm for a structured head is unreachable behind `!hit`; harmless.
- Not judged, as before: a registry-injected column and a leaf on an object outside the stack.
- Public surface: no export added, renamed or removed in `packages/lint`. The return type that gained `what` belongs to a closure-local function. `packages/spec` gains one ledger entry and no schema, key or describe change.
- Migration ledger: one new semantic entry, id `lookup-filter-record-path-structured-refused`. Its content is right; the step it is filed under is wrong (M1 in ④).

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: no (narrowing) — present line-initial in the PR body and in the changeset, with `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` beside it; the two agree.

- `@objectstack/lint` minor: matches a `narrowed` kind on the package whose verdict changes.
- `@objectstack/spec` patch: matches what the diff publishes from spec, one ledger entry and no schema change. Same level as the ledger-only spec line of #37910; the predecessor #34489 took spec minor because it also edited describes.
- Gate verdict: `Check Changeset` success on the head (run 140858748287, completed 04:09Z). The failure listed on the same head (140844648873, 03:11Z) is the earlier run against the PR body before its `Clause-②` line was corrected; the later run supersedes it.
- N1 (nit) — the PR title and the changeset headline read `fix(lint):` with no `!`, while the changeset declares `(narrowing)`, which AGENTS.md calls BREAKING, and both lookup precedents (#34489, #37910) carry the `!`. No gate reads it red.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev flag, `composite` and `record` kept: answered, right (see ①).
- Dev flag, the hint reused verbatim ("a multi-valued field holds a list") on a structured refusal: accepted deviation. The card's item asks for "the same hint as the multi-valued refusal"; the sentence still gives the correct fix. The PR body's "per the ruling" cites nothing: the card thread carries no ruling, only that item.
- Dev flag, the verdict says `a structured field` without the type name: accepted; the field and object are named, and the type is one lookup away.
- Dev flag, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` not measured locally: answered by the head's check-runs, all green.
- `open_questions` of report 7232219858 (where the ledger entry lands; the `Clause-②` arm): both answered by the seat's amendment 7232237546. The first answer named the filename with the `18.` prefix, which is where M1 comes from. Report 7233729062 carries none.
- The card's "Decide with the spec lane whether the same rule refuses it": no separate decision is on the card. This record is that judgment: the same rule should refuse it (④).
- The card's "Measure first": done, 18 `$record` hits at 815e882b, none a `lookupFilters` path to a structured field. Not re-run here.
- "Read from code, the picker compares that object as one value" (changeset, ledger `reason`): the picker is not in this repository and I could not read it. What this tree does establish is the server half: an object or list is outside the accepted comparand set. The claim is worded as inference, which is what it is.
- SQL push-down: not applicable. The change is an in-memory judgment over the object graph; no query, no id materialisation, no join.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing makes the spec's own refusal real; it does not take a declared capability away. On `main`, `LookupFilterRecordReferenceSchema` says a `$record` reference "stands for ONE value of the record being edited" and pairs only with the six scalar comparisons, and the spec's cross-field table already says a `STRUCTURED_JSON_TYPES` column is not one comparable value. No sentence of the published spec promises that a path to an address, a location, a JSON document, a repeater or a vector resolves to a comparand. The refusal sits beside the multi-valued one, uses the same two positions and the same predicate source the rest of the platform reads. Attempts to break it (a hop through a structured head, a structured head that is also multi-valued, an injected or out-of-stack leaf, a scalar field beside structured ones) all come out as the tests pin them.

M1 (must-fix) — the ledger entry is filed under protocol major 18, and it belongs to 19. The file is `semantic/18.lookup-filter-record-path-structured-refused.ts`, so `gen:migration-registry` places it in `step18`. On this head `PROTOCOL_VERSION` is `19.0.0` (moved by #37314 on 2026-11-26), the package is `19.0.0-next.2` in changesets pre mode, and the 18.x line is released through 18.6.0, so this refusal first ships in 19. `composeMigrationChain(fromMajor, toMajor)` keeps only the steps above `fromMajor`: an author on 18.6.0 who runs `os migrate meta --from 18` gets step 19 alone and is never shown this entry, although that upgrade is exactly where the refusal starts. That is the silence ADR-0087 D3 exists to prevent, and the changeset's `adr-0087: registered` marker then claims a notice that upgrade does not deliver. The entries README names the file by protocol major, `step19`'s own docstring says later retirements on the v19 line add their entries there, and 16 of the 19 semantic entries added since the protocol move are `19.` files, including the sibling lookup refusal of #37910. The precedent was right to use 18: it shipped in 18.6.0 while 18 was the open line. Copying its prefix after the protocol moved is not. No gate catches this: `check-adr-0087-registration` reads the id, not the major. Fix: rename the file to `19.lookup-filter-record-path-structured-refused.ts`; the id, the entry body and the changeset marker stay as they are. The seat's amendment 7232237546 names the `18.` filename, so the file surface needs the same one-character correction.

S1 (should-fix) — the two texts that enumerate what this rule refuses at `$record` are now incomplete, and the predecessor updated both in its own PR. `rule-explanations.ts` (the `os lint --explain object-field-ref-unknown` text) says a resolving path "is refused too when it reads a list", naming only multi-valued fields. The spec describes in `field.zod.ts` (`LookupFilterRecordReferenceSchema` and `lookupFilters[].value`, which generate the reference page `content/docs/references/data/field.mdx`) say the same. An author refused for an address path who asks the rule to explain itself, or reads the reference, finds no such refusal. The claim's file surface forbade both files while other open PRs held them, which explains the gap and does not close it. Fix here, or name a follow-up card in the PR body; either way the texts should take the set from the same sentence the hand-written docs now use.

N2 (nit) — "holds an object" in the ledger `reason`, the changeset and the source comments is loose for three members: `repeater` and `vector` hold lists, and `json` is open. `relationships.mdx` already says it accurately ("a list or an object rather than one value").

Out of diff, for a follow-up card and not findings on this head: three other entries landed under `18.` after the protocol move (two in #37366, one in #37513) and have the same exposure as M1; and a single `file` or `image` field is in neither refused set although the spec's cross-field table gives that family no comparison class either.

Tests: the new block derives its 14 head and leaf cases from the spec set itself, asserts the full message and hint, and carries a control and the hop-through case. `Test Core` is green on the head.

Reviewed-by: `session_017xRBcSAaBEfQpU2yJexSJ8`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `9a9f0e6421d9675916ebe74684004b1d3d8f6a00`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/lint/src/validate-object-field-refs.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/19.lookup-filter-record-path-structured-refused.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-object-field-refs.test.ts + read, not reviewed: packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/README.md, packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts.template, packages/spec/src/migrations/chain.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/protocol-version.ts, packages/spec/src/data/field-value.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/filter-cross-field-comparison-class.ts

Delta review of record 7233848869 (FAIL on c0deeb35). Inputs: the delta `c0deeb35..9a9f0e64` (one commit, three files), the PR body and title as they stand, card #34562's two new comments (claim amendment 7233891050, os-dev-report 7234837890), follow-up card #38141, and the check-runs on this head. Everything the earlier record judged right and the delta does not touch stands as written there.

M1: closed
S1: closed

### ① Derived judgments

- Migration ledger: the entry file is renamed to `semantic/19.lookup-filter-record-path-structured-refused.ts`, so the generator places it in `step19`, and no `18.` copy remains in the tree at this head. With `PROTOCOL_VERSION` at `19.0.0`, an author upgrading from the released 18.x line now meets the entry on the hop where the refusal starts. Right.
- The entry's id, `surface`, `replacement` and `acceptanceCriteria` are byte-identical to the previous head. `reason` differs only by the "a list or an object rather than one value" wording and its line wrapping; I compared the two strings clause by clause and found no other change.
- Accept set: unchanged by the delta. The two hunks in `validate-object-field-refs.ts` are comment text only; the predicate, the message and the hint are untouched, and the test file is not in the delta.
- Public surface: unchanged by the delta.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: no (narrowing) — unchanged in the PR body and the changeset, with `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`.

- Levels unchanged: `@objectstack/lint` minor, `@objectstack/spec` patch. The delta publishes nothing that moves either.
- N1 is taken: the changeset headline and the PR title both read `fix(lint)!:`.
- Gate verdict: `Check Changeset` success on this head twice, run 140869171213 (04:52Z) and the re-run after the title and body edit, 140881198072 (05:45Z). `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Test Core`, `Dogfood Regression Gate` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` are success; the head shows 62 success, 12 skipped, no failure and nothing pending.

### ③ Boundary flags

- The carrier for the earlier should-fix: the PR's `Acceptance notes` line names follow-up #38141. That is the second of the two routes the earlier record offered, and the card is fit for it: open, it names both texts (`rule-explanations.ts` and the two describes in `field.zod.ts`), states the expected sentence and the regenerated reference page, and is `Blocked-by: #38096`, which is the right order since the texts describe a refusal that exists only once this PR lands. Accepted.
- Out-of-diff observation from the earlier record (other `18.` entries filed after the protocol move): carried on #38142 per the claim amendment and the PR body. I did not read #38142; it is not a finding on this head either way.
- The dev's probe that the landed multi-valued `18.` entry is absent from the chain for an 18.x upgrade is consistent with what `chain.ts` reads as; it belongs to #38142, not here.
- The dev re-ran only the ledger, spec and lint families locally this round and says so. The head's check-runs cover the rest.
- `open_questions` in report 7234837890: none.
- Still open as accepted deviations, unchanged: the reused hint sentence on a structured refusal, and the PR body's "per the ruling", which still cites nothing on the card.
- SQL push-down: not applicable; the delta is a file rename and prose.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

The design judgment of the earlier record stands: the narrowing makes the spec's own refusal real and takes no declared capability away. The delta changes nothing about the refusal. It moves the ledger notice to the step whose upgrade it belongs to, which was the one contract defect on the previous head.

N2 is taken: the ledger comment and `reason`, the changeset and both source comments now say "a list or an object rather than one value", matching `relationships.mdx`.

Nothing new is introduced by the delta. I looked for a stale `18.` reference to the new entry in the changeset, the PR body and the file's own comment, and found none; the comment's mention of the multi-valued entry by id is correct, since that entry keeps its own name.

Reviewed-by: `session_017xRBcSAaBEfQpU2yJexSJ8`

**VERDICT: PASS**

### ⛔ merge queue 构建失败 — 先分诊，再决定要不要重排

队列构建 [46114012154](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/46114012154) 红了。队列跑的是**全量**套件（PR 侧 CI 只跑 affected 子集），
所以失败的测试可能在本 PR 没碰过的包里 —— 那不是重排能修的。每次盲目重排都会让排在后面的所有 PR 重建一轮。

**分类：`failure`** —— 按下面的日志分诊。

**失败的 job（日志抽取，best effort）：**

- **[Dogfood Regression Gate (2/3)](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/46114012154/job/140883774061)** — 失败步骤: Boot example apps and exercise real user flows

  ```
  @objectstack/dogfood:test:  FAIL   isolated  test/approval-decide-over-mcp.dogfood.test.ts > an approver's agent decides a pending approval request over MCP (#32442) > ⭐ a member on no slate is refuse
    ↳ 失败原因: @objectstack/dogfood:test: AssertionError: {
  @objectstack/dogfood:test:  FAIL   isolated  test/approval-decide-over-mcp.dogfood.test.ts > an approver's agent decides a pending approval request over MCP (#32442) > ⭐ [#33690] the approver's call d
    ↳ 失败原因: @objectstack/dogfood:test: AssertionError: {
  @objectstack/dogfood:test:  FAIL   isolated  test/approval-decide-over-mcp.dogfood.test.ts > an approver's agent decides a pending approval request over MCP (#32442) > ⭐ [#33690] the submitter's recal
    ↳ 失败原因: @objectstack/dogfood:test: AssertionError: {
  @objectstack/dogfood:test:  FAIL   isolated  test/mcp-system-object-action-exposure.dogfood.test.ts > [#27681, #27900] sys_user identity actions over MCP: what each bucket's declaration lets an agent 
    ↳ 失败原因: @objectstack/dogfood:test: AssertionError: {
  @objectstack/dogfood:test:  FAIL   isolated  test/mcp-system-object-action-exposure.dogfood.test.ts > [#27681, #27900] sys_user identity actions over MCP: what each bucket's declaration lets an agent 
    ↳ 失败原因: @objectstack/dogfood:test: AssertionError: {
  ```

> `↳ 失败原因` 是判读的关键：**超时**（`Test timed out in …` / `Hook timed out in …`）多半是负载/时序，不是本 PR 的回归；
